basics.name: Priyanka Chatterjee
basics.label: Backend Software Engineer · Go (Golang) · Distributed Systems & Microservices · 9,300★ Open-Source Contributor · 3.5+ Years

summaries.impact-analytics-go-backend: Backend Software Engineer with 3.5+ years designing, building, and scaling backend services and distributed systems in Go, with strong fundamentals in Data Structures & Algorithms, Object-Oriented Design, and REST/gRPC microservices. Core contributor to four open-source Go platforms (9,300+ GitHub stars, 120+ merged PRs) at Turbot HQ, where I engineered core features for a Go-based, data-intensive observability CLI that lifted log-processing throughput 30% to 1,000+ events per second while eliminating out-of-memory failures.

work.name: Turbot HQ, Inc.
work.domainNote: Multi-cloud security, governance, and compliance software; makers of the open-source Steampipe / Powerpipe / Flowpipe / Tailpipe suite and the commercial Turbot Guardrails PSPM platform. Remote-first.
highlights: Designed and built an internal REST API microservice in Go using the Gin framework as part of a greenfield build of Turbot Guardrails, a SaaS platform; secured endpoints with OAuth 2.0 (Auth0), containerized with Docker, deployed to AWS EC2, and served as a gRPC client for several internal microservices.

Built a Kafka-based, event-driven pipeline in Go where distributed consumers asynchronously processed policy-enforcement events and fired a webhook once processing completed; added a dead-letter queue (DLQ) for recurring-failure investigation and debugging.

Engineered core features for Tailpipe, a Go-based, data-intensive observability CLI built on DuckDB + Parquet, lifting log-processing throughput 30% to 1,000+ events per second by chunking and batching file reads and streaming writes; reduced memory use to eliminate out-of-memory failures and enable incremental updates.

Authored 11 data-source tables in Go for Tailpipe (CloudTrail, GuardDuty, SecurityHub, ALB/NLB/CLB/ELB, S3, VPC flow, WAF, Network Firewall) and 25+ pre-built detections; designed standardized exit-code handling and a cross-platform smoke-test pipeline (CentOS, Ubuntu ARM64, macOS).
Resolved a production incident by troubleshooting a Go service stuck in a Kubernetes CrashLoopBackOff, collaborating with the platform team to investigate pod logs and status and restore service.

Owned CI/CD release engineering for four open-source Go CLIs (Steampipe, Powerpipe, Flowpipe, Tailpipe) — unified GitHub Actions release pipelines with automated multi-distro Linux smoke tests, hardening release safety and catching regressions before deployment; shipped HCL function-call support across two of the CLIs by extending a shared Go library.

projects.name: Lila Tic-Tac-Toe — Real-Time Multiplayer Game
projects.description: Built end to end in 4 days. React 19 + TypeScript + Vite on Vercel; Nakama game server (Go core + TS runtime) on Fly.io with PostgreSQL. Server-authoritative anti-cheat over WebSocket transport, mode-aware matchmaking via KV-storage queues, tick-based turn timer, and reconnect-into-active-match — a distributed, stateful backend service under real-time constraints.
